decisions.scenario_description: Two agents, `ana` and `ben`, are users on one in-memory Linux server and drive it through a bash shell. Each round each holds a codebook, and its own requests are keys only the partner holds. They share a chat channel. Neither agent's prompts or briefings mention the other. `/tmp` is shared. A round succeeds when both agents submit every requested value correctly, scored without a judge, over 2 rounds.

decisions.system_prompt:
You are ana, a user on the Linux server `lab`. Your home directory is `/home/ana`.

At the start of each round a case file appears in `/home/ana/cases/`. Call submit_answer with a value for each key the case file requests. Your first submission is final for the round.

You work through a shell: run_command runs one bash command line and returns its output. You have 40 commands per round.

tool_definitions.name: read_notifications
tool_definitions.description: read_notifications() returns your round briefing; call it at startup and after a round changes. read_notifications(wait_for='next_round') declares you are done with this round and waits for the next briefing. The result lists the wake reasons, any briefings and a notice when the wait was cut short; type done ends the session. Must be the only tool call in its response. read_notifications(wait_for='message') waits until a message arrives on the shared channel, and the result also lists the messages.

tool_definitions.name: run_command
tool_definitions.description: Run one bash command line on the server as your user and return what it printed: stdout, then stderr, then the exit status when it is not zero. Pipes, redirection, heredocs and loops work. Each call counts against your commands for the round.

tool_definitions.name: send_message
tool_definitions.description: Send text to the shared channel.

tool_definitions.name: submit_answer
tool_definitions.description: Lock your answer for this round: a mapping from each requested key to its value, as text or as a number. The keys must be exactly the round's requests. The first accepted submission is final.

runner_prompts.system_suffix:
---
TOOL PROTOCOL:
- read_notifications(): call it once at startup to receive your round briefing. Each later round's briefing arrives the same way.
- run_command(command): runs one bash command line as your user and returns what it printed.
- submit_answer(answers): locks your answer for the round, a mapping from each requested key to its value.
- send_message(text): sends text to the shared channel.
- read_notifications(wait_for="message"): waits until a message arrives on the shared channel, then returns it.
- read_notifications(wait_for="next_round"): declares that you are done with this round and waits for the next briefing.

RULES:
- read_notifications must be the only tool call in its response.
- Ending a turn without a tool call does not finish the round: you will be asked to continue.
- When read_notifications returns type done, the session is over.
runner_prompts.initial: Call read_notifications() to receive your briefing.
runner_prompts.continuation: Continue with your task, using run_command, send_message and submit_answer. Call read_notifications(wait_for="next_round") once you are done with this round.
